title: The Cech complex of a covering on a site
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and $\mathcal U=\{f_t:U_t\to U\}_{t\in T}$ a covering of $\mathcal C$. (a) *Fibre products.* For $p\ge0$ and $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_p)\in T^{p+1}$, a fibre product $U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$ is an object $W$ with morphisms $\mathrm{pr}_k:W\to U_{t_k}$ ($0\le k\le p$) such that $w=f_{t_k}\circ\mathrm{pr}_k:W\to U$ does not depend on $k$, universal among such data: for every object $Z$ and morphisms $a_k:Z\to U_{t_k}$ with $f_{t_0}a_0=\cdots=f_{t_p}a_p$ there is exactly one $a:Z\to W$ with $\mathrm{pr}_k\circ a=a_k$ for all $k$ (for $p=0$, $W=U_{t_0}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_0=\mathrm{id}$). Such a fibre product exists for every $\mathbf t$ (by axiom (iii) of a site and induction on $p$), is unique up to unique isomorphism compatible with the $\mathrm{pr}_k$, and one, $U_{\mathbf t}=U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_p}$, is chosen for every $\mathbf t$. (b) *Index maps.* For $\mathbf t\in T^{p+1}$ and a map $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,q\}\to\{0,\ldots,p\}$ let $\mathbf t\alpha=(t_{\alpha(0)},\ldots,t_{\alpha(q)})\in T^{q+1}$ and let $\alpha^*:U_{\mathbf t}\to U_{\mathbf t\alpha}$ be the unique morphism with $\mathrm{pr}_k\circ\alpha^*=\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha(k)}$ for all $k$. For $0\le j\le p+1$ let $\delta_j:\{0,\ldots,p\}\to\{0,\ldots,p+1\}$ be the increasing injection omitting $j$; for $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_{p+1})$, $\delta_j^*:U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_{p+1}}\to U_{t_0}\times_U\cdots\times_U\widehat{U_{t_j}}\times_U\cdots\times_UU_{t_{p+1}}$ is the *projection omitting the $j$-th factor*. (c) *The Cech complex.* Let $\mathcal F$ be a presheaf of abelian groups on $\mathcal C$, i.e. an object of the abelian category $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$ of functors $\mathcal C^{op}\to\textit{Ab}$ [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact]; for $h:V\to W$ write $s\mapsto s|_V=\mathcal F(h)(s)$. The *Cech complex* $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is the cochain complex of abelian groups [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\prod_{\mathbf t\in T^{p+1}}\mathcal F(U_{\mathbf t})$ for $p\ge0$ (componentwise addition; $s_{t_0\ldots t_p}$ denotes the component of $s$ at $(t_0,\ldots,t_p)$), $\check{\mathcal C}^p=0$ for $p<0$, and differential $d=d^p:\check{\mathcal C}^p\to\check{\mathcal C}^{p+1}$, $d(s)_{t_0\ldots t_{p+1}}=\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^j\mathcal F(\delta_j^*)\big(s_{t_0\ldots\hat{t_j}\ldots t_{p+1}}\big)$ for $p\ge0$ (restriction along the projection omitting the $j$-th factor), $d^p=0$ for $p<0$; $d$ is a group homomorphism and $d\circ d=0$. (d) *Cech cohomology.* $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=H^p(\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F))=\ker d^p/\operatorname{im}d^{p-1}$ ($p\ge0$; so $\check H^0(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)=\ker d^0$), the *Cech cohomology groups* of $\mathcal F$ with respect to $\mathcal U$. (e) *Functoriality and exactness.* A morphism $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of presheaves of abelian groups induces the morphism of complexes $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\varphi)=\prod_{\mathbf t}\varphi_{U_{\mathbf t}}$, $(\check{\mathcal C}^p(\varphi)s)_{\mathbf t}=\varphi_{U_{\mathbf t}}(s_{\mathbf t})$, and hence maps $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\varphi)$; this makes $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-):\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\textit{Ab})$ an additive functor, and $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$ additive functors $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)\to\textit{Ab}$. The functor $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)$ is exact: if $\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''$ is exact at $\mathcal F$ in $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$, then $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F')\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F'')$ is exact for every $p$; in particular a short exact sequence of presheaves goes to a short exact sequence of complexes. (Stacks Cohomology on Sites, Section 03AK, Definition 03AM, Section 03AO, Lemma 03AQ. General-site version of [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex], which is stated for the small etale site.)

proof.text: *Existence of the fibre products (a).* Induction on $p$. For $p=0$, $U_{t_0}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_0=\mathrm{id}$ is a fibre product: given $a_0:Z\to U_{t_0}$, $a=a_0$ is the only morphism with $\mathrm{id}\circ a=a_0$. Let $p\ge0$, $\mathbf t=(t_0,\ldots,t_{p+1})$, and let $(V,\mathrm{pr}_0,\ldots,\mathrm{pr}_p)$ be a fibre product of $(t_0,\ldots,t_p)$ (induction hypothesis), with $v=f_{t_k}\mathrm{pr}_k:V\to U$. Since $\mathcal U$ is a covering and $v:V\to U$ is a morphism, axiom (iii) of a site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] (Sites, Definition 00VH (3)) says that the fibre product $U_{t_{p+1}}\times_UV$ of $f_{t_{p+1}}$ and $v$ exists; call its projections $q:U_{t_{p+1}}\times_UV\to U_{t_{p+1}}$, $r:U_{t_{p+1}}\times_UV\to V$. Put $W=U_{t_{p+1}}\times_UV$, $\mathrm{pr}_k=\mathrm{pr}_k\circ r$ for $k\le p$ and $\mathrm{pr}_{p+1}=q$. Then $f_{t_k}\mathrm{pr}_k=v r=f_{t_{p+1}}q$ for all $k$. Universality: given $a_k:Z\to U_{t_k}$ ($k\le p+1$) with all $f_{t_k}a_k$ equal to $c:Z\to U$, the universal property of $V$ gives a unique $b:Z\to V$ with $\mathrm{pr}_kb=a_k$ ($k\le p$), and $vb=f_{t_0}a_0=c=f_{t_{p+1}}a_{p+1}$, so there is a unique $a:Z\to W$ with $ra=b$, $qa=a_{p+1}$; it satisfies $\mathrm{pr}_ka=a_k$ for all $k$. If $a'$ is another such morphism, then $\mathrm{pr}_k(ra')=a_k$ for $k\le p$ gives $ra'=b$ by uniqueness for $V$, and $qa'=a_{p+1}$, so $a'=a$ by uniqueness for $W$. Uniqueness of fibre products up to unique isomorphism compatible with the $\mathrm{pr}_k$ is the usual argument for limits (two universal objects map to each other, and the composites are identities by the uniqueness clause); a fibre product $U_{\mathbf t}$ is chosen for every $\mathbf t$ (axiom of choice; $T$ and the $T^{p+1}$ are sets).

source.place: Sites, Definition 00VH (definition-site) condition (3); Cohomology on Sites, Section 03AK ('any covering of a site is a family ... to which the definition applies', after Definition 03AM)

proof.text: *Index maps (b).* For $\mathbf t\in T^{p+1}$ and $\alpha:\{0,\ldots,q\}\to\{0,\ldots,p\}$, the morphisms $\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha(k)}:U_{\mathbf t}\to U_{t_{\alpha(k)}}$ ($0\le k\le q$) satisfy $f_{t_{\alpha(k)}}\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha(k)}=w$ for all $k$, so the universal property of $U_{\mathbf t\alpha}$ (step 1) gives exactly one $\alpha^*:U_{\mathbf t}\to U_{\mathbf t\alpha}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_k\alpha^*=\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha(k)}$. Functoriality: $\mathrm{id}^*=\mathrm{id}$, and for $\beta:\{0,\ldots,r\}\to\{0,\ldots,q\}$ one has $\beta^*\circ\alpha^*=(\alpha\circ\beta)^*:U_{\mathbf t}\to U_{\mathbf t\alpha\beta}$, since $\mathrm{pr}_k\beta^*\alpha^*=\mathrm{pr}_{\beta(k)}\alpha^*=\mathrm{pr}_{\alpha(\beta(k))}$ for every $k$ and a morphism into $U_{\mathbf t\alpha\beta}$ is determined by its composites with the projections. The projection omitting the $j$-th factor is $\delta_j^*$, $\delta_j(k)=k$ for $k<j$ and $\delta_j(k)=k+1$ for $k\ge j$; it is the restriction map of the Stacks formula (equation-d-cech).

source.place: Section 03AK (section-cech), the projection map after equation 03AL (equation-d-cech)

proof.text: *The differential and $d\circ d=0$ (c).* Each $\mathcal F(\delta_j^*)$ is a group homomorphism and the components of $d(s)$ are sums of them applied to components of $s$, so $d$ is a homomorphism of the product groups. Let $s\in\check{\mathcal C}^p$, $p\ge0$, and $\mathbf t\in T^{p+3}$. By definition, and since $\mathcal F$ is a contravariant functor with $\mathcal F(\delta_i^*)\circ\mathcal F(\delta_j^*)=\mathcal F(\delta_j^*\circ\delta_i^*)=\mathcal F((\delta_i\circ\delta_j)^*)$ (step 2; here $\delta_j:\{0..p\}\to\{0..p+1\}$, $\delta_i:\{0..p+1\}\to\{0..p+2\}$), $d(d(s))_{\mathbf t}=\sum_{i=0}^{p+2}\sum_{j=0}^{p+1}(-1)^{i+j}\mathcal F((\delta_i\delta_j)^*)(s_{\mathbf t\delta_i\delta_j})$. The cosimplicial identity $\delta_i\circ\delta_j=\delta_{j+1}\circ\delta_i$ for $0\le i\le j\le p+1$ holds because both sides are the increasing injection $\{0,\ldots,p\}\to\{0,\ldots,p+2\}$ whose image omits exactly $i$ and $j+1$. The map $(i,j)\mapsto(j+1,i)$ is a bijection from $\{(i,j):0\le i\le j\le p+1\}$ onto $\{(i',j'):0\le j'<i'\le p+2\}$ (inverse $(i',j')\mapsto(j',i'-1)$), and the two sets partition the index set of the double sum. Matched terms have the same composite $\delta_i\delta_j=\delta_{j+1}\delta_i$, hence the same tuple $\mathbf t\delta_i\delta_j$ and the same restriction map, and opposite signs $(-1)^{i+j}$ and $(-1)^{i+j+1}$; so $d(d(s))_{\mathbf t}=0$. In degrees $p<0$, $d\circ d=0$ trivially. Hence $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is a cochain complex of abelian groups in the sense of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] (objects $\check{\mathcal C}^p$, $p\in\mathbf Z$, with $d^{p+1}d^p=0$). (Stacks: 'It is straightforward to see that $d\circ d=0$'; this is that verification. For the small etale site the same complex is the Mathlib leaf of [def-weil-pbc-cech-complex], where Mathlib obtains $d\circ d=0$ from the alternating coface complex of a cosimplicial object, i.e. from the same identities.)

source.place: Section 03AK (section-cech): equation 03AL (equation-d-cech) and the sentence after it ('It is straightforward to see that d o d = 0')

proof.text: *Independence of the choices.* If $U'_{\mathbf t}$ are other choices of fibre products, step 1 gives unique isomorphisms $\iota_{\mathbf t}:U'_{\mathbf t}\to U_{\mathbf t}$ with $\mathrm{pr}_k\iota_{\mathbf t}=\mathrm{pr}'_k$, and $\alpha^*\iota_{\mathbf t}=\iota_{\mathbf t\alpha}\alpha'^*$ (both have components $\mathrm{pr}'_{\alpha(k)}$). Hence $s\mapsto(\mathcal F(\iota_{\mathbf t})(s_{\mathbf t}))_{\mathbf t}$ is an isomorphism of complexes between the two Cech complexes, commuting with the differentials term by term and natural in $\mathcal F$; so the complex, and $\check H^p$, are well defined up to canonical isomorphism.

*Cech cohomology and functoriality (d), (e).* $\check H^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)$ is the $p$-th cohomology object $H^p=\ker d^p/\operatorname{im}d^{p-1}$ of the cochain complex of step 3 [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]; since $\check{\mathcal C}^{-1}=0$, $\check H^0=\ker d^0$. For $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$, $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\varphi)$ is a homomorphism and commutes with $d$: for $\mathbf t\in T^{p+2}$, $(d\,\check{\mathcal C}^p(\varphi)s)_{\mathbf t}=\sum_j(-1)^j\mathcal G(\delta_j^*)\varphi_{U_{\mathbf t\delta_j}}(s_{\mathbf t\delta_j})=\sum_j(-1)^j\varphi_{U_{\mathbf t}}\mathcal F(\delta_j^*)(s_{\mathbf t\delta_j})=(\check{\mathcal C}^{p+1}(\varphi)\,ds)_{\mathbf t}$ by naturality of $\varphi$ and additivity of $\varphi_{U_{\mathbf t}}$. Clearly $\check{\mathcal C}(\mathrm{id})=\mathrm{id}$, $\check{\mathcal C}(\psi\varphi)=\check{\mathcal C}(\psi)\check{\mathcal C}(\varphi)$ and $\check{\mathcal C}(\varphi+\psi)=\check{\mathcal C}(\varphi)+\check{\mathcal C}(\psi)$ (componentwise, the addition of presheaf morphisms being sectionwise [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact]); so $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)$ is an additive functor $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)\to\mathrm{CoCh}(\textit{Ab})$, and composing with the cohomology functors $H^p$ of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives the functors $\check H^p(\mathcal U,-)$, additive since $H^p$ of a sum of morphisms of complexes is the sum of the induced maps on $\ker d^p/\operatorname{im}d^{p-1}$.

*Exactness (e)* (Lemma 03AQ). Let $\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{a}\mathcal F\xrightarrow{b}\mathcal F''$ be exact at $\mathcal F$ in $\textit{PAb}(\mathcal C)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact], for every $\mathbf t$ the sequence $\mathcal F'(U_{\mathbf t})\to\mathcal F(U_{\mathbf t})\to\mathcal F''(U_{\mathbf t})$ is exact. A product of sequences $A_{\mathbf t}\xrightarrow{a_{\mathbf t}}B_{\mathbf t}\xrightarrow{b_{\mathbf t}}C_{\mathbf t}$ of abelian groups exact at $B_{\mathbf t}$ is exact at $\prod B_{\mathbf t}$: the composite is $0$ componentwise, and if $(y_{\mathbf t})$ has $b_{\mathbf t}(y_{\mathbf t})=0$ for all $\mathbf t$, choose $x_{\mathbf t}$ with $a_{\mathbf t}(x_{\mathbf t})=y_{\mathbf t}$, then $(x_{\mathbf t})\mapsto(y_{\mathbf t})$ (in Mathlib: products in AddCommGrpCat are exact, instance instAB4StarAddCommGrpCat, Mathlib/Algebra/Category/Grp/AB.lean:98). Hence $\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F')\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal U,\mathcal F'')$ is exact for every $p\ge0$ (and trivially for $p<0$). For a short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F''\to0$ (exact at each of the three places) this gives the short exact sequences $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal F')\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^p(\mathcal F'')\to0$ for all $p$ (the functor is additive, so it sends the zero presheaf to the zero complex), and by [lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact] (2) $0\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F')\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F)\to\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,\mathcal F'')\to0$ is short exact in $\mathrm{CoCh}(\textit{Ab})$; so the additive functor $\check{\mathcal C}^\bullet(\mathcal U,-)$ is exact in the sense of Homology, Lemma 010N (4).

split_report.summary: Checked against Stacks Cohomology on Sites Section 03AK (equation 03AL, Definition 03AM, the remark that coverings of a site qualify), Section 03AO (equation 03AP) and Lemma 03AQ, Sites Definition 00VH (3), Homology Lemma 010N. Made the definition self-contained in five parts: (a) iterated fibre products U_t0 x_U ... x_U U_tp defined by their universal property (wide pullback), existence by axiom (iii) and induction, a choice fixed; (b) index maps alpha^* for arbitrary maps of index sets and the face projections delta_j^*; (c) the complex, zero in negative degrees, with the sign convention of 03AL; (d) Cech cohomology ker/im; (e) functoriality and exactness. Six steps: the induction for the fibre products (on def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology), functoriality of alpha^* (elementary), d o d = 0 written out from the cosimplicial identity delta_i delta_j = delta_{j+1} delta_i (i <= j) with the cancelling bijection of index pairs, independence of the choices (elementary), functoriality in F and the functors H^p (on def-weil-abstract-derived-category), and exactness 03AQ (on the new Mathlib leaf lem-weil-pbc-abelian-presheaves-evaluation-exact for exactness of evaluation in PAb, the product of exact sequences of abelian groups written out (Mathlib form AB4Star AddCommGrpCat recorded), and the reviewed leaf lem-weil-pbc-cochain-complexes-degreewise-exact). def-weil-pbc-cech-complex is not cited as a dependency: it is the same construction for the small etale site and cannot be specialized to a general site; it is mentioned in the text only.
